title: How Snake Handlers Work
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck explore snake handling, starting with a casual discussion of personal snake encounters and safe snake relocation tips (extension tools, strike distances). They cover non-religious handlers (zoo/show handlers, rescuers, venom milkers, and the need for a second person present), then the history of Holiness serpent handling beginning with George Hensley in 1910 in Tennessee, its spread through Appalachia, legal status and raids (including Jamie Coots' church in 2008), and Hensley's death from a bite in 1955. They discuss the 2013 Nat Geo show Snake Salvation, the mistreatment and malnourishment of handled snakes and why bites may be less dangerous, and then Bill Haast, his Miami Serpentarium, self-immunization with venom, and his long life. The episode closes with a Facebook listener questions segment (part one).

segments.title: Opening sponsor reads and banter
segments.summary: Squarespace and Crown Royal sponsor reads, plus hosts' casual banter about hair, beards, and TV ads.

segments.title: Introduction to snake handling and religious background
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode's religious snake handling topic, express concern for handlers' safety, and discuss church culture and personal snake encounters.

segments.title: Snake Salvation and Jamie Coots
segments.summary: Discussion of the 2013 National Geographic show Snake Salvation, pastor Jamie Coots who died of a rattlesnake bite after the show ended, and Andrew Hamblin, who wanted to bring snake handling into mainstream Christianity.

segments.title: Types of snake handlers and safe snake removal
segments.summary: Overview of non-religious handlers: display handlers, veterinarians, and rescue professionals. Hosts discuss extension tools and advice for relocating snakes, with a personal anecdote about relocating a snake from a backyard.

segments.title: Snake strike distance and safety rules
segments.summary: Rules of thumb on how far snakes can strike relative to body length, advice to approach snakes calmly, and a warning not to touch unidentified snakes; anti-venom timing discussed.

segments.title: Venom milking and free-handling
segments.summary: Explanation of venom milking, its value to research labs, how venom is extracted through a membrane, free-handling techniques, and the need for a second person present.

segments.title: Dangers of venom and constrictors
segments.summary: Discussion of tissue damage and organ failure from venom, the Texas coral snake's pain molecule, constrictor dangers, and the need for extra people when handling large snakes, plus a zookeeper death anecdote.

segments.title: History of Holiness serpent handling
segments.summary: George Hensley's 1910 start in Tennessee at Dolly Pond Church of God, his Bible-based philosophy, spread through Appalachia, and his death from a bite in 1955 after refusing treatment.
topics: Church of God with Signs Following

segments.title: Legal status, raids, and animal welfare of religious handlers
segments.summary: Practice continues in Appalachia; state laws exist but are rarely enforced due to religious freedom; 2008 stings including Coots' church; hosts discuss mistreatment and malnourishment of snakes and why bites may be less harmful.

segments.title: Bill Haast and the Miami Serpentarium
segments.summary: Profile of Bill Haast, self-trained herpetologist who ran the Miami Serpentarium, self-immunized with snake venom, supplied his blood as antivenom, and lived to 100. The serpentarium closed in 1984 after a 1977 accident that injured a boy.

segments.summary: Brief Facebook listener questions segment and closing remarks on contact channels.
